A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Advantage Alignment Algorithms. The complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C support comparison, including matching content across pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments on four game environments, with quantitative comparisons, training curves, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their quantitative and qualitative results in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 and the main objectives in Equations 8–10 are unchanged. New Appendix A.9 explains the n-player formulation, but v2 already includes a sum over opponents in Equation 66 and seven-agent experiments. The formula corrections do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma, Coin Game, continuous Negotiation Game, and Commons Harvest Open environments and scenarios. Appendix A.9 adds mathematical exposition without additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same participants: LOQA, POLA, MFOS, AC, AD, and Random in Coin Game; AC, AD, PPO, and PPO-SR in Negotiation Game; and the same Commons Harvest baselines. Appendix C’s compared variants are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported metrics, training budgets, architectures, trajectory lengths, checkpoint selection, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Section 5 newly states that fixed learned policies are evaluated zero-shot against a policy distribution; this clarifies the existing evaluation rather than reporting a protocol revision.

E4.justification: The same trajectory case studies, negotiation training curves, Coin Game gradient-component masking ablations, and Commons Harvest analyses at beta values 0.5, 1, and 2 remain. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Figure 1’s ten-seed averages and one-standard-deviation whiskers, the same league evaluation counts, and Commons Harvest’s best-of-ten-seeds selection followed by 100 evaluations. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The numerical results, curves, and qualitative trajectories in Figures 1–8 are unchanged. Examples include AdAlign’s Coin Game self-play return of 0.28, Negotiation Game self-play return of 0.35, and Commons Harvest average normalized return of 1.63.

T1.justification: v3 restores omitted beta factors in Equation 7 and Appendix A.1, and gamma^(t-k) in Equation 62, improving consistency with existing final formulas. New Appendix A.9 explicitly presents n-player gradient and PPO-advantage expressions, building on Equation 66. The three theorem statements and their proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about Advantage Alignment, connections to LOLA and LOQA, continuous-action support, scalability, cooperation, and resistance to exploitation. Nash-equilibrium preservation remains the same claim.

C2.justification: The mechanism interpretations and qualifications are retained, including negotiation-training instability in Appendix B.3 and the cooperation-versus-exploitability tradeoff between Commons Harvest strategies in Appendix C.3. No substantive interpretation or limitation is added.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly specifies that evaluation holds the learned policy fixed and tests it zero-shot against a distribution of policies, following LOQA. This adds reproducibility information. Appendix B’s architectures, hyperparameters, hardware, runtimes, and implementation disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work discussion are unchanged. The additional citation to already-cited LOQA attributes the evaluation protocol without changing the paper’s novelty claims or substantive research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds short explanations, an explicit advantage definition, Appendix A.9, and acknowledgements, alongside limited wording corrections and updated publication headers. The main narrative and section organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figure 3’s caption corrects the cooperation colour from green to blue, matching the unchanged illustration. The negotiation reward formula becomes inline, and acknowledgements cause reference reflow. Figures and table structures otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Restoring omitted scaling and discount factors improves consistency with the existing objectives. The n-player explanation, explicit fixed-policy evaluation disclosure, and corrected Figure 3 caption also reduce ambiguity. New Equation 67 contains a theta_1/theta_i index mismatch, limiting the mathematical polish. Overall, these are useful but modest improvements; empirical evidence and core conclusions are unchanged.
